docs.title: HumemDB
docs.text:
HumemDB is an embedded multi-model runtime that keeps each engine doing the job it is already good at.

  • SQLite is the canonical OLTP and write path.
  • DuckDB is the analytical read path.
  • Cypher is lowered over SQLite-backed graph storage.
  • Vector search spans exact and ANN paths, with exact NumPy over SQLite-backed collections today.

The current public surfaces are intentionally explicit:

  • query_type="sql" means HumemSQL v0.
  • query_type="cypher" means HumemCypher v0.
  • query_type="vector" means HumemVector v0.
  • route="sqlite" or route="duckdb" selects the execution backend.

docs.title: Why HumemDB exists
docs.text: HumemDB is not trying to force OLTP, analytics, graph traversal, and vector retrieval through one engine just because that sounds elegant. The current runtime starts with a thin orchestration layer over embedded engines so correctness stays obvious and routing stays visible.

docs.title: What is shipped today
docs.text:
• Portable PostgreSQL-like SQL translation for a narrow SELECT / INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / CREATE subset.
  • SQLite-backed graph tables with narrow Cypher CREATE and MATCH flows.
  • Vector search with an exact SQLite-plus-NumPy baseline today and room for indexed ANN paths where the benchmark justifies them.
  • Explicit transaction control per route.

docs.title: What is intentionally out of scope for v0
docs.text:
• Full PostgreSQL compatibility.
  • Full Cypher compatibility.
  • Automatic routing.
  • Indexed ANN as the default vector path.
  • A broad internal IR before mixed-mode composition actually requires it.

docs.title: Writing rules
docs.text:
• keep the docs aligned with the actual v0 runtime surface
  • prefer clear boundaries over aspirational claims
  • add examples only for tested behaviors

docs.title: HumemDB license
docs.text:
HumemDB's own source code is licensed under MIT.

  • Repository license file: LICENSE
  • Package metadata: pyproject.toml

That MIT grant applies to HumemDB's code and documentation in this repository. It does not automatically relicense third-party dependencies.

docs.title: Runtime libraries HumemDB relies on
docs.text:
The current runtime depends on a small set of explicit Python libraries and embedded engines:

  • sqlite3 from the Python standard library for the canonical local write path
  • duckdb for analytical reads
  • numpy for the exact in-memory vector search baseline
  • sqlglot[c] for the SQL translation layer
  • lancedb for benchmark work and future indexed ANN paths
  • threadpoolctl for thread-pool coordination

HumemDB intentionally presents those libraries as part of the implementation story instead of pretending everything comes from one hidden backend.

docs.title: Third-party licenses
docs.text:
Third-party dependencies keep their own licenses and distribution terms.

  • Installing HumemDB may download third-party wheels or source distributions.
  • Some of those dependencies may include native code or platform-specific wheels.
  • Those components remain under their upstream licenses.

For the concrete dependency set used by this project, see:

  • pyproject.toml
  • uv.lock

If you need a formal license review for a deployment, review the resolved dependency set from the lockfile rather than only the top-level MIT license.

docs.title: Release Workflow
docs.text:
HumemDB's public release path currently centers on two outputs:

  • the PyPI package
  • the versioned docs site

docs.title: Package release
docs.text:
Package versions come from Git tags that match the Hatch VCS pattern:

v0.1.0
v0.1.1
v0.2.0

The PyPI workflow builds the package, checks metadata, verifies the wheel installs, and publishes through PyPI trusted publishing.

docs.title: Docs release
docs.text:
The docs deployment workflow:

  • checks out humemdb
  • installs the docs dependencies
  • checks out humemai-docs
  • runs mike deploy with the humemdb prefix
  • optionally updates the latest alias

docs.title: Shared docs hub
docs.text: The shared docs landing page at https://docs.humem.ai/ links to both product doc sets. HumemDB is published as a separate section instead of being mixed into the ArcadeDB tree.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
HumemDB ships real Python examples in the repository examples/ directory, and the docs pages in this section describe those exact files.

Like the ArcadeDB docs, each page is intended to be a companion to the real Python script, not a disconnected hand-written snippet.

Current shipped examples:

  • 01 - SQL Basics: generates 2,000 users and 50,000 orders, then runs both SQLite and DuckDB queries.
  • 02 - Cypher Social Graph: generates thousands of graph nodes and edges with richer properties.
  • 03 - Vector Search: generates 36,000 vectors across two collections and exercises exact search.

Run them locally from the repository root:

uv sync
uv run python scripts/release/run_examples.py

Or run individual files directly:

uv run python examples/01_sql_basics.py
uv run python examples/02_cypher_social_graph.py
uv run python examples/03_vector_search.py

docs.title: 01 - SQL Basics
docs.text:
View source code

This page documents the real repository example examples/01_sql_basics.py.

docs.title: What the Python example does
docs.text:
The script generates a moderately sized embedded workload instead of a tiny hand-made toy dataset.

  • 2,000 users
  • 50,000 orders
  • 2 SQLite tables
  • transactional bulk inserts through the public API
  • SQLite filtered OLTP-style reads
  • SQLite joined reads
  • DuckDB grouped analytical reads over the SQLite-backed tables

docs.title: Why this example exists
docs.text: HumemDB is supposed to route small transactional work and broader analytical work to different engines explicitly. This example demonstrates that split using the actual public Python API.

docs.title: Main operations covered
docs.text:
• CREATE TABLE routed to SQLite
  • executemany(...) inside an explicit transaction
  • ILIKE translation on the SQLite route
  • SQLite join queries for row-oriented reads
  • DuckDB grouped aggregate queries for broader scans

docs.title: Representative flow
docs.text:
with HumemDB("app.sqlite3", "analytics.duckdb") as db:
    db.query(
        "CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, segment TEXT NOT NULL, city TEXT NOT NULL)",
        route="sqlite",
    )
    db.query(
        "CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, user_id INTEGER NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total_cents INTEGER NOT NULL)",
        route="sqlite",
    )

    with db.transaction(route="sqlite"):
        db.executemany(..., users, route="sqlite")
        db.executemany(..., orders, route="sqlite")

    sqlite_rows = db.query(..., route="sqlite")
    duckdb_rollup = db.query(..., route="duckdb")

docs.title: Supported statement kinds
docs.text:
• SELECT
  • INSERT
  • UPDATE
  • DELETE
  • CREATE

docs.title: Explicit rejections
docs.text:
• recursive CTEs
  • unsupported PostgreSQL syntax outside the current tested surface
  • direct public writes routed to DuckDB

docs.title: 02 - Cypher Social Graph
docs.text:
View source code

This page documents the real repository example examples/02_cypher_social_graph.py.

docs.title: What the Python example does
docs.text:
The script builds a generated social/work graph rather than a tiny three-node toy.

  • 5,000 repeated graph patterns
  • thousands of nodes
  • thousands of directed KNOWS edges
  • richer node properties: name, age, active, cohort, city
  • richer relationship properties: since, strength, and implicit type
  • SQLite and DuckDB graph reads over the same stored graph state

docs.title: Main operations covered
docs.text:
• repeated CREATE graph writes on the SQLite route
  • named parameters in Cypher CREATE
  • relationship alias returns
  • reverse-edge matching
  • WHERE ... AND ... filters
  • ORDER BY and LIMIT

docs.title: Representative flow
docs.text:
db.query(
    (
        "CREATE (a:User {name: $a_name, age: $a_age, active: $a_active, cohort: $cohort, city: $city})"
        "-[r:KNOWS {since: $since_one, strength: $strength_one}]->"
        "(b:User {name: $b_name, age: $b_age, active: $b_active, cohort: $cohort, city: $city})"
    ),
    route="sqlite",
    query_type="cypher",
    params={...},
)

docs.title: Supported today
docs.text:
• labeled node creation
  • single directed relationship creation
  • narrow MATCH flows
  • relationship aliases
  • reverse-edge matching
  • WHERE equality predicates joined by AND
  • ORDER BY and LIMIT
  • named parameters such as $name

docs.title: Not promised yet
docs.text: HumemDB does not claim broad Cypher compatibility today. The current surface is the tested subset described above, and unsupported constructs should fail clearly instead of being guessed at.

docs.title: 03 - Vector Search
docs.text:
View source code

This page documents the real repository example examples/03_vector_search.py.

docs.title: What the Python example does
docs.text:
The script generates a sizable exact-search workload rather than only a handful of vectors.

  • 24,000 vectors in the default collection
  • 12,000 vectors in the archive collection
  • 16 dimensions per vector
  • multiple logical buckets
  • exact search through search_vectors(...)
  • exact search through raw query_type="vector"
  • cache invalidation after inserting additional vectors

docs.title: Why this example matters
docs.text: HumemDB currently positions the public vector runtime as an exact SQLite-plus-NumPy baseline. That claim is not very useful if the only shipped example uses three points. This example exercises tens of thousands of generated points while staying inside the current public v0 surface.

docs.title: Representative flow
docs.text:
with HumemDB("vectors.sqlite3") as db:
    db.insert_vectors(build_default_vectors())
    db.insert_vectors(build_archive_vectors())

    result = db.search_vectors(
        "default",
        _embedding(1.0, 0.0, 0.0),
        top_k=5,
        metric="cosine",
    )

docs.title: What this means in practice
docs.text:
• SQLite is the canonical vector store.
  • The public path is exact, not ANN.
  • Bucket filters can narrow the candidate set before scoring.
  • Collection caches are invalidated automatically after SQL writes that touch vector storage.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
• cosine
  • dot
  • l2

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.10 or newer.
  • A normal local Python environment managed with uv.

docs.title: SQL
docs.text:
from humemdb import HumemDB

with HumemDB("app.sqlite3", "analytics.duckdb") as db:
    db.query(
        "CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL)",
        route="sqlite",
    )

    with db.transaction(route="sqlite"):
        db.executemany(
            "INSERT INTO users (id, name) VALUES (?, ?)",
            [(1, "Alice"), (2, "Bob")],
            route="sqlite",
        )

    result = db.query(
        "SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY id",
        route="sqlite",
    )

    print(result.columns)
    print(result.rows)

docs.title: Cypher
docs.text:
from humemdb import HumemDB

with HumemDB("graph.sqlite3", "graph.duckdb") as db:
    db.query(
        "CREATE (a:User {name: 'Alice'})-[:KNOWS]->(b:User {name: 'Bob'})",
        route="sqlite",
        query_type="cypher",
    )

    result = db.query(
        "MATCH (a:User)-[:KNOWS]->(b:User) RETURN a.name, b.name",
        route="sqlite",
        query_type="cypher",
    )

    print(result.rows)

docs.title: Vector search
docs.text:
from humemdb import HumemDB

with HumemDB("vectors.sqlite3") as db:
    db.insert_vectors(
        [
            (1, "default", 0, [1.0, 0.0]),
            (2, "default", 0, [0.9, 0.1]),
            (3, "default", 1, [0.0, 1.0]),
        ]
    )

    result = db.search_vectors(
        "default",
        [1.0, 0.0],
        top_k=2,
        metric="cosine",
    )

    print(result.rows)

docs.title: Read the surface boundaries
docs.text: These examples are deliberately simple because the public v0 surfaces are still intentionally narrow. Before building on a query mode, check the guide pages for what is supported and what HumemDB still rejects explicitly.

docs.title: Benchmarks
docs.text: Benchmarks are part of the routing story, not an afterthought.

docs.title: Relational benchmark
docs.text:
HUMEMDB_THREADS=8 python scripts/benchmarks/duckdb_direct_read.py --rows 50000
HUMEMDB_THREADS=8 python scripts/benchmarks/duckdb_direct_read.py \
    --rows 10000000 --warmup 1 --repetitions 5 --batch-size 50000

Current takeaway:

  • SQLite stays stronger for point lookups and smaller filtered reads.
  • DuckDB wins broader grouped scans and analytical aggregates.

docs.title: Graph benchmark
docs.text:
HUMEMDB_THREADS=8 python scripts/benchmarks/cypher_graph_path.py --nodes 5000 --fanout 3
HUMEMDB_THREADS=8 python scripts/benchmarks/cypher_graph_path.py \
    --nodes 1000000 --fanout 4 --tag-fanout 2 --warmup 1 --repetitions 5 --batch-size 20000

Current takeaway:

  • SQLite is very strong for selective graph traversal.
  • DuckDB becomes compelling only once the read broadens into graph-analytic shapes.

docs.title: Vector benchmark
docs.text: The vector benchmark scripts measure exact NumPy search and quantized variants so later routing choices can be based on observed crossover points instead of guesswork.

docs.title: Query Surfaces
docs.text: HumemDB treats SQL, Cypher, and vector search as separate frontends.

docs.title: HumemSQL v0
docs.text:
• PostgreSQL-like source syntax.
  • Translated with sqlglot into backend SQL.
  • Public writes go to SQLite.
  • Read queries may go to SQLite or DuckDB.

docs.title: HumemCypher v0
docs.text:
• Separate frontend, not a SQL dialect.
  • Graph data is stored in SQL tables.
  • Cypher reads can run on SQLite or DuckDB.
  • Cypher writes still go to SQLite.

docs.title: HumemVector v0
docs.text:
• Separate frontend, not forced SQL syntax.
  • SQLite-backed vector table.
  • Exact NumPy search over cached matrices.
  • Routing is currently fixed to route="sqlite".

docs.title: Why the version label matters
docs.text: The v0 marker is attached to the language surfaces, not to the package version. A package release can move forward while a surface is still intentionally narrow and allowed to change incompatibly.

docs.title: Routing
docs.text: HumemDB starts with explicit routing because hidden routing rules would make the first release hard to reason about.

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
• sqlite: canonical write path and transactional source of truth
  • duckdb: analytical read path over SQLite-backed data

docs.title: Current policy
docs.text:
• send writes to SQLite
  • allow read-only SQL on DuckDB
  • allow Cypher reads on SQLite or DuckDB
  • keep vector search on SQLite

docs.title: Why explicit routing comes first
docs.text: Automatic routing is planned later, but the runtime needs benchmark evidence and stable surface semantics before it should guess for the caller.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
result = db.query(
    "SELECT kind, COUNT(*) AS total FROM events GROUP BY kind",
    route="duckdb",
)

If that same call were a write, HumemDB would reject it instead of silently mutating the analytical replica.

docs.title: Transactions
docs.text: Transaction control is explicit and route-scoped.

docs.title: Context manager
docs.text:
with db.transaction(route="sqlite"):
    db.query(
        "INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)",
        route="sqlite",
        params=("Alice",),
    )

On normal exit, the transaction commits. If an exception escapes the block, HumemDB rolls the selected route back before the exception continues.

docs.title: Manual control
docs.text:
db.begin(route="sqlite")
try:
    db.query("UPDATE users SET active = 1", route="sqlite")
    db.commit(route="sqlite")
except Exception:
    db.rollback(route="sqlite")
    raise

docs.title: Batch writes
docs.text: executemany(...) is intentionally limited to SQLite for now. That keeps the initial bulk-write story simple and aligned with the current source-of-truth model.

docs.title: Vectors
docs.text: The current vector surface is deliberately conservative.

docs.title: Storage model
docs.text:
• vectors are stored in SQLite as float32 blobs
  • one collection is loaded as one NumPy matrix
  • dimensions must be consistent within a collection

docs.title: Search model
docs.text:
• exact search only on the public path
  • optional bucket filtering before scoring
  • metrics: cosine, dot, l2

docs.title: Why exact search is the default
docs.text: HumemDB needs a defensible baseline before it broadens into indexed ANN routing. The exact SQLite plus NumPy path is simple enough to benchmark honestly and strong enough to set the first public contract.

docs.title: Relationship to LanceDB
docs.text: LanceDB is in the dependency set because benchmark and future accelerated work already exists around that direction. It is not the default public runtime path today.
